atlas-se.0001: Strong graduate employment and the Nordic start-up leader: Stockholm holds about half of Sweden’s information-and-communication jobs and nearly two-thirds of its finance jobs, with Spotify, Klarna, SEB and Handelsbanken; Gothenburg is Volvo’s city. Corporate graduate programmes recruit in English but many roles need Swedish, youth unemployment is high at 24.3%, and since June 2026 non-EU students may work only 15 hours a week in term.
atlas-se.0003: Eurostat’s employment counts are for metropolitan regions and for 2021; Statistics Sweden’s city-level employment by industry was not read.
atlas-se.0004: No source gives graduate entry pay by field or city; the pay figures are all-employee regional averages from Statistics Sweden.
atlas-se.0005: Swedbank, Ericsson, H&M and AstraZeneca are not listed as employers because no source we can cite was read.
atlas-se.0006: Graduate programme calendars were read only for SEB and Nordea; none was found for Spotify, Klarna, Handelsbanken or Volvo.
atlas-se.0007: No family is rated in Uppsala: Eurostat does not put it second or third in the country for ICT or finance jobs, and its strength is the university, which is not a graduate-employer family.
atlas-se.0008: Sweden: graduate market, pay after rent, expert tax relief, permits, SEB and Nordea programmes

atlas-se.0029: The Ministry of Finance’s nine-month trainee programme for recent graduates has its next recruitment round in spring 2027, and Volvo Group’s 12-month Finance Graduate Program recruits next in autumn 2027.
atlas-se.0030: Swedbank’s Analyst Development Trainee Program, for recent graduates in industrial economics, mathematics, economics, statistics or computer science, lasts over 10 months; applications are closed and open again in January 2027.
atlas-se.0031: English is widely used in international workplaces in Sweden, but Swedish is an advantage and in many roles a requirement; CVs should be in the language of the job posting.
atlas-se.0032: Sweden’s expert tax relief (25% of pay exempt for seven years) excludes anyone resident in Sweden in the previous five years, so it does not help someone who studied there.
atlas-se.0033: Of SSE’s 2025 master’s class, 40% went into consulting, 29% into finance and 9% into technology, with first employers including McKinsey, BCG, SEB, Handelsbanken, Swedbank, Klarna and H&M; over 60% started their careers in Sweden and 38% of international graduates stayed.
atlas-se.0034: SEB’s International Trainee Programme runs every other year from September; the 2026–27 intake closed on 11 January 2026, and some roles require Swedish.
atlas-se.0035: AB Volvo has its headquarters in Gothenburg.
atlas-se.0036: Eurostat counts 629,000 people in work in the Malmö metropolitan region in 2021: 25,000 in information and communication (third in Sweden, after Stockholm and Gothenburg) and 8,000 in finance and insurance (third in Sweden, after Stockholm and Gothenburg). The region’s GDP was €62.3 billion in 2021.
atlas-se.0037: Eurostat counts 178,000 people in work in the Uppsala metropolitan region in 2021: 5,000 in information and communication and 1,000 in finance and insurance. The region’s GDP was €19.1 billion in 2021.
atlas-se.0038: Eurostat counts 1,316,000 people in work in the Stockholm metropolitan region in 2021, 117,000 of them in information and communication (53% of Sweden’s 221,000) and 68,000 in finance and insurance (64% of 107,000).
atlas-se.0039: Eurostat counts 870,000 people in work in the Gothenburg metropolitan region in 2021, 33,000 of them in information and communication (15% of Sweden’s 221,000) and 10,000 in finance and insurance (9% of 107,000).
atlas-se.0040: Spotify gives its address as Regeringsgatan 19, Stockholm, as its headquarters, with entities in 16 countries.
atlas-se.0041: Klarna gives its address as Sveavägen 46, Stockholm, and says it supports 26 countries.
atlas-se.0042: Handelsbanken gives its head office as Kungsträdgårdsgatan 2, Stockholm, and says it has more than 12,000 employees.
atlas-se.0043: Volvo Group says it has 99,000 employees, production in 17 countries and sales in 180 markets, with its headquarters in Gothenburg; Volvo Car Group gives Gunnar Engellaus väg 8, Gothenburg.
atlas-se.0044: Axis Communications gives Lund as its headquarters and says it has around 5,000 employees in over 50 countries.
atlas-se.0045: Uppsala University says it has 50,000 students and 7,539 staff (year average, 6,648 full-time equivalents).
atlas-se.0046: In the QS World University Rankings 2027 (18 June 2026) Lund University is 71st, KTH 82nd, Uppsala University 87th and Stockholm University 167th, the first four in Sweden.
atlas-se.0047: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Stockholm 35th of 117 centres, the twelfth European centre after London, Zurich, Geneva, Luxembourg, Lugano, Paris, Copenhagen, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Dublin and Edinburgh, and 17th for fintech; Gothenburg is an associate centre with too few assessments to be ranked.
atlas-se.0048: Startup Genome’s 2026 Top 40 ranks Stockholm 23rd in the world, level with Amsterdam-Delta and up eight places, the standout European performer; its Europe chapter names Amsterdam, Munich and Stockholm as the top tier after London, Paris and Berlin and puts Stockholm fourth in Europe for AI-native value ($5.8 billion, after London, Paris and Munich); the Stockholm page shows an ecosystem value of $56 billion against a global average of $25 billion.
atlas-se.0049: Startup Genome’s Gothenburg ecosystem page shows an ecosystem value of $2 billion, $120 million of seed and Series A funding in 2023–2025 and $1 billion of exits, against global averages of $25 billion and $554 million.
atlas-se.0050: In 2025 ICT specialists were 8.9% of employment in Sweden, the highest of the 33 European countries Eurostat lists (EU 5.0%, Luxembourg 8.7%, Finland 7.8%).
atlas-se.0051: In 2025, 91.1% of Swedish tertiary graduates aged 20–34 who finished within the last three years were in work (EU 85.3%), but unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds was 24.3% (EU 15.2%), the highest of the Nordic countries.
atlas-se.0052: In 2025 the average monthly salary of all employees was SEK 42,900 in Sweden, SEK 48,300 in the Stockholm region, SEK 42,300 in West Sweden (Gothenburg), SEK 41,700 in South Sweden (Malmö) and SEK 40,500 in East-Central Sweden (Uppsala).
atlas-se.0053: Swedish hiring leans on contacts: many posts are filled through networks and referrals before they reach a job site, so career guides tell students to ask guest speakers for informational talks and go to alumni and industry evenings. Business graduates of the top school sign early: 80% of SSE’s master’s class accepted a job before graduating.
atlas-se.0055: SSE has more than 100 corporate partners and about a third of its graduates start with one of them.
atlas-se.0056: Stockholm University tells students that internships help them understand Swedish workplace culture and recommends a master’s thesis written with a company, authority or organisation. Handelsbanken takes students into part-time jobs alongside their studies and lists thesis and internship options, and the Government Offices take unpaid interns of about 20 weeks twice a year.
atlas-se.0058: Banks and industrial groups run trainee programmes with winter windows for an August or September start: SEB’s international programme took applications from November 2025 to January 2026 and runs every other year; Swedbank’s analyst programme (over 10 months) reopens in January 2027; Volvo Group runs a 12-month finance and a 15-month operations and engineering programme and welcomes 100+ graduates a year.
atlas-se.0059: The Ministry of Finance runs a nine-month trainee programme for recent graduates with a permanent post from the start; its next round is in spring 2027.
atlas-se.0060: Stockholm University says many jobs in Sweden are filled through networking rather than public adverts; it points students to guest speakers, classmates, alumni and career fairs. Informational interviews and LinkedIn contacts with alumni fill the posts that are never advertised.
atlas-se.0061: Invest in Gothenburg advises personalised LinkedIn requests to peers and people in the target department, not asking strangers for jobs.
atlas-se.0062: Expat.com says most vacancies are advertised online, with LinkedIn and company career pages the most widely used; Arbetsförmedlingen’s Platsbanken is open to everyone, but many international or specialist private-sector roles are advertised elsewhere.
atlas-se.0063: This is also the route for the experienced hire: hiring slows in July, is mixed in August and picks up from September.
atlas-se.0064: KTH lists 15 career fairs, led by Armada; LTH’s ARKAD brings about 200 companies and organisations to Lund over two days in November; Stockholm University runs career events and Chalmers works with Unimeet Gothenburg on company visits and a Career Day.
atlas-se.0066: Academic Work, founded in Sweden in 1998 for students and young professionals, has either recruitment jobs (you are employed by the client) or consultant jobs (you are employed by Academic Work and placed at a client); postings open to English speakers are tagged “Jobs in English”.
atlas-se.0067: Expat.com says agencies matter mainly for specialised roles such as tech or finance, and are optional for most expats.
